description: Repairs r-sort-3b/memo-index-ddl: the memo set could not show 255-unit truncation: it holds an exact duplicate (A x255 + x at IDs 7 and 15) and the eight rows MI took include the case-equal pair a and A, so the unique-index refusals (3022) came from real duplicates; and every statement ran on one shared table, so an earlier index or refusal could affect the next. New General ACCDB. MI(ID Long primary key, MK MEMO, TK TEXT(255)) holds 10 values that are all different under General compare: a, b, A x255, A x255 + x, A x255 + y, A x256 + x, A x254 + B, A x254 + C, e-acute x256 + p and + q (TK is MK cut to its first 255 units). Each of 7 statements runs on its own fresh copy of MI (CREATE TABLE and INSERT..SELECT), in its own read/write open with dbFailOnError, DBEngine.Errors after it and an image kept after the close: CREATE INDEX and CREATE UNIQUE INDEX on MK, MK DESC, (TK, MK) and (MK, TK); ADD CONSTRAINT UNIQUE (MK); and CREATE INDEX on TK as the control. Then, each on its own copy, DAO TableDef.CreateIndex with a field MK appended to a non-unique, to a unique and to a primary index (TableDefs refreshed before Item, DBEngine.Errors after Indexes.Append), and the three tables MI3, MI4 and MI5 whose MEMO column is a primary key or has a unique constraint (column and table form). The refreshed index metadata of every table is read after its step. Asks whether a memo column can be a native key in any route, which refusal each route gives, and whether the key is cut at 255 units.
